issues.problem: The prediction question is asked before the frame that shows the query state, so students cannot see the answer in the visualization when asked.
issues.fix: Move the setState to frame 10 before the speech that asks the prediction, or ask the prediction at frame 11 where the subtraction is visible.

issues.problem: The answer beat (frame 11) is skipped in the scripted narration, so the key formula P[r+1] − P[l] is never explicitly shown in the main flow.
issues.fix: Add a setState to frame 11 and a speech line with the answer narration before jumping to frame 12.

issues.where: Code map for C++ and Python
issues.problem: Pseudocode line 4 (the query function) is mapped to the function signature line rather than the line that actually computes the answer.
issues.fix: Map pseudocode line 4 to C++ line 6 and Python line 5, or split the pseudocode into a signature line and a return line.

issues.problem: The narration says 'Với q truy vấn dài ta mất O(n·q)' but does not explain why this is bad in the main narration; the hint does explain it.
issues.fix: Add a short clause in the narration such as 'quá chậm khi n và q lớn' to make the motivation explicit.

issues.problem: The narrated path skips the answer beat (frame 11): after the predict question it jumps from the query setup (frame 10) straight to the final result (frame 12), so the key subtraction P[r+1] − P[l] is never shown or spoken and the predict question is never explicitly resolved in narration. It is also inconsistent with the negative/n1 presets, which do narrate the answer beat, and with the stated truncated semantics (narratedBeats=12 of 13, yet the skipped beat is not the last one).
issues.fix: Narrate frame 11 with the answer speech (e.g. 'Lấy P[6] − P[2] = 23 − 4 = 19…') before frame 12; if a beat must be cut, drop one of the eight identical build beats instead of the answer reveal.

issues.problem: 'Trừ P[l − 1] … còn mất phần tử a[l − 1]' / 'it also drops a[l − 1]' is ambiguous and easily read as the result losing a[l−1]; in fact P[r+1] − P[l−1] keeps a[l−1], so the result is too large — it is P[l−1] itself that does not contain a[l−1].
issues.fix: Rephrase to state the direction explicitly, e.g. 'P[l−1] không chứa a[l−1] nên kết quả bị thừa a[l−1]' / 'P[l−1] does not include a[l−1], so the result wrongly keeps a[l−1]'.

issues.problem: range_sum rebuilds the whole prefix array inside every call, so each query costs O(n); called for q queries this degenerates to O(n·q) — the exact complexity the lesson says to avoid — and contradicts the 'build P once, then O(1) per query' message.
issues.fix: Split the code into a build-once part (e.g. a make_prefix(a) function or a captured P) and a query that only computes P[r+1] − P[l], or add a comment noting P must be built once outside the query loop.

issues.problem: The naive direct-sum frame points at pseudocode line 4 'query(l, r):', but the direct-summation loop being explained is not in the pseudocode at all, so the highlighted line does not match what is being 'executed'.
issues.fix: Either add the naive summation loop to the pseudocode so it can be highlighted, or leave codeLine unset for the naive frame.

issues.where: frames index 1 (all presets) and beats naive/done
issues.problem: Big-O notation (O(n), O(1), O(n·q), O(n+q)) is used from the second frame onward without any definition, which may lose grade 8-9 students who have not met it.
issues.fix: Add a one-line gloss at first use, e.g. 'O(n) nghĩa là số phép tính tỉ lệ với n'.
